capability: END-TO-END integration demo: coating candidate design card for 5 canonical DGEBA-based epoxy-amine formulations (IPDA, m-XDA, DDS, TETA, DETA). Each candidate receives Tg prediction (ML + Van Krevelen physical), Hansen 3-component δ_d/δ_p/δ_h partial parameters, Hansen chi vs 3 solvents (water, ethanol, chloroform), applicability domain Tanimoto score, and a chemistry-motivated composite marine-coating-suitability score. Portfolio produces ACTIONABLE output. 4/5 candidates correctly flagged out-of-AD; only IPDA passes all gates with composite score 0.645. Grants no batch-release, manufacturing-qualification, optimizer, or product-performance authority.

coating_suitability_composite_formula.note: Chemistry-motivated composite for marine anti-corrosion epoxy-amine coatings; higher = better

population: 5 canonical DGEBA-based epoxy-amine coating formulations from May 1988 Epoxy Resins Ch. 6: IPDA, m-XDA, DDS, TETA, DETA. Each with a coating-industry context describing typical use (marine, aerospace, concrete-lining, industrial-maintenance, general-purpose).
split_methodology: Integrated end-to-end pipeline: (1) Load Polyuniverse Epoxy 1M, sample 100k with seed=0, scaffold-safe 60% train fold. (2) Fit Morgan-only HistGBM Tg model. (3) For each of 5 candidates: predict ML Tg + Van Krevelen physical Tg, compute Hansen δ_d/δ_p/δ_h via Van Krevelen 21-group table, compute Hansen chi vs 3 solvents, compute AD Tanimoto to training scaffold set, output composite suitability score.
theory: May 1988 Epoxy Resins Chemistry and Technology 2nd ed. Ch. 6
Wicks, Jones, Pappas 2007 Organic Coatings 3rd ed. Ch. 24 (marine coating design)
Hansen 2007 Hansen Solubility Parameters 2nd ed. CRC
Van Krevelen 1990 Properties of Polymers 3rd ed. Ch. 6 & 7
Flory 1953 Principles of Polymer Chemistry Ch. XII
